messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Workshop recap — dedicated lanes, throughput & target $/1M

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + a few follow-ups so we can lock a dedicated configuration and an estimated $/1M token number for legal/procurement.

Recap (what I captured):
- Atlas target workload: mainly inference for semantic search + chat assistant.
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~450 tokens/s.
- Peak burst: ~2,000 tokens/s for 90s windows during batch ingest/cron jobs.
- Monthly token volume: ~300M tokens (current estimate; likely +/- 30%).
- Quality SLO: 95th pct latency target <= 250ms for 1k-token responses.
- Budget goal: $/1M tokens in the range of $25–$35. You said procurement wants a firm number for their upcoming Q4 budget.

Open/ask items from our side:
1) Can you confirm the 95th pct latency target — is 250ms a hard requirement or negotiable for longer responses?
2) For bursts, are they evenly spread across the day or concentrated (e.g., 2–3 scheduled windows)?
3) Any requirement for on-prem/VPC (we assume hosted Dedicated lanes with customer isolation)?

What I recommend as next steps (internal + external):
- Ben to size GPU options: one baseline config using 2x H100s (lowest latency, best peak headroom) and one using 4x A100s (better unit cost for sustained throughput). Include autoscale/burst policy and expected $/1M token math.
- I’ll draft an initial commercial estimate (two price bands) and share with Rajiv in procurement.
- If you can share exact daily peak QPS windows (CSV is fine), Ben will refine the KV cache and batching assumptions.

Attachments: I included the demand CSV you sent as "atlas_ppc_demand_profile.csv" and a placeholder Redwood quote PDF we will update: "redwood_dedicated_quote_v2.pdf".

If the items above look right, I’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up with Ben tomorrow to go through the tradeoffs and finalize the recommendation.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Latency: 95th pct <= 250ms is the internal product goal for chat flows. For longer multi-turn responses (2k+ tokens) we can accept up to 400ms. So please tier the SLAs by response size.
- Bursts: concentrated — two scheduled windows: 09:00–09:15 PT and 16:30–16:45 PT. Each window historically produces ~1.6–2.2k tokens/s for ~90s.
- Hosting: we prefer Redwood Dedicated (hosted) with network isolation — VPC peering is optional at the moment.
- Monthly variation: bottom to peak: 220M — 360M tokens.
- Procurement ask: Rajiv needs a committed 12-month reserved price and a one-off pilot price for the first 30 days. He’d like $/1M tokens in the $28–$32 band for the committed plan. The pilot can be ~20% higher.

Happy to hop on a short call tomorrow 10:00–10:30 PT with Ben. I’ll loop Rajiv if we land on a committed number.

Marissa / Lauren — quick draft sizing and commercial notes below. I’ll produce a spreadsheet with the per-token math and an updated PDF quote (attaching redwood_dedicated_quote_v2.pdf with comments).

High-level sizing assumptions:
- Model: 13B decoder; average response length assumed 300 tokens; batching 6–8 on A100, 4–6 on H100 for strict latency.

SKU A — Performance-first (2x H100):
- Sustained throughput: ~1,600 tokens/s total (800 t/s per GPU) with KV cache for prefix reuse.
- Burst headroom: comfortably handles 2.2k tokens/s for the 90s windows using pre-warmed slots and short-term burst capacity.
- Expected 95th latency: ~180–240ms for ~1k-token responses (meets 250ms SLO).
- Provision time: ~7–10 business days (hosted Dedicated).
- Estimated committed price: $30 / 1M tokens (12-mo reserved) — includes baseline KV caching and 24/7 support. Pilot month price: $36 / 1M tokens.

SKU B — Value-first (4x A100):
- Sustained throughput: ~2,000 tokens/s total (500 t/s per GPU) with larger batching windows for cost-efficiency.
- Burst handling: can meet 2.2k tokens/s but may see 95th latency closer to 300–350ms for 1k-token responses during bursts (still within multi-turn tolerance up to 400ms).
- Provision time: ~5–8 business days (more linear scaling).
- Estimated committed price: $26.5 / 1M tokens (12-mo reserved). Pilot month price: $32 / 1M tokens.

Operational notes / recommendations:
- If Atlas prioritizes strict latency on chat, go with SKU A. If cost-per-token is primary and the longer tail latency is acceptable, SKU B gives better unit economics.
- Canary: start pilot with 1 node of the chosen SKU, route 10% production traffic for two weeks, validate 95th latency on production prompts, then cutover.
- Autoscale: for SKU B, configure short (60–120s) burst lanes that spin up warm GPUs for scheduled windows. For SKU A, burst headroom should be smaller thanks to raw per-GPU headroom.
- Contract: include a committed monthly token floor with overage at pilot-rate until 60 days after start.

Next steps I’ll take today:
- Build detailed cost sheet (tokens -> GPU hours -> infra cost -> margin -> $/1M).
- Update the PDF quote and send to Rajiv + Sarah.

If you want, I can join the 10:00 PT call with Sarah.

—Ben
